newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-panel says Cyprus rights record improves.
newsitem.headline: Euro-panel says Cyprus rights record improves.

text.p: Cyprus has made great strides towards ending torture and other violations of human rights since 1992, the European Committee Against Torture said in a report published on Thursday.
Not one case of torture was reported to the committee during a visit to Cyprus in May 1996, the report said.
That compared to a 1992 trip when it was made aware of several actions, most of them committed in police stations, including hanging detainees by their feet, electric shock and beatings.
The committee is part of the 40-member Council of Europe, of which Cyprus is a member, and the report was approved by the Cyprus government before its release.
The 1992 report had singled out police headquarters in Limassol for the harshest treatment and Larnaca, on a lesser scale. Both cities are on the island's southern coast.
"There has been a very positive evolution since our first visit, notably concerning people detained by the police," the committee said.

But it said it was aware that there were still some cases of mistreatment by the authorities and it reiterated its earlier criticism of the duration of police custody, which can be extended to as long as three months on a judge's request.

It also repeated its disapproval of Cyprus's policy of separating inmates infected with AIDS or Hepatitis B from other prisoners, regardless of their condition. "There is no medical justification for this segregation," it said.

The committee, whose experts were allowed unrestricted access to military and psychiatric institutions as well as prisons, said human rights in general had improved in Cyprus since a mediator was named in 1994 to hear complaints of torture and mistreatment brought by individuals.
